newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO's MeesPierson probes U.S. fund.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO's MeesPierson probes U.S. fund.

text.p: ABN AMRO's investment banking unit MeesPierson said on Friday it was investigating an unnamed U.S. investment fund for which it acted as a sales agent.
MeesPierson spokesman Paul Fentrop said this followed the discovery of "certain things that we put question marks by", but he declined to elaborate.
He also said this would not affect the proposed acquisition of MeesPierson by Dutch-Belgian insurance group Fortis.
Fortis, which two weeks ago signed a letter of intent to buy MeesPierson from ABN AMRO, said it was aware of the irregularities.
Fentrop said MeesPierson started an investigation eight days ago after discovering irregularities involving a securitisation fund in the United States.
He said investors who bought into the fund through MeesPierson had been informed of the probe.
But he declined to say if anyone had lost money.
"We know of the irregularities," said Fortis spokesman Kees Leering, adding that Fortis was proceeding with the due diligence process as part of the proposed purchase.
